questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have taught myself Italian and wanted to try to become more or less fluent while just in general enjoying the exchange experience. Bologna seemed to be the perfect choice of an Italian student city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy to be honest

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a few pages on the university's website to orient myself. Otherwise I mainly figured things out by myself through people I met through initiatives like ESN.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing in Bologna is comparatively expensive and difficult to find so try to start early.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most of the action happens in the city center but it is more expensive to live centrally and with access to a bike the entire city is quite quickly navigable so it might be an idea to look for housing outside the medieval walls.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Difficult to find out which class were when and where to register my arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I tried to mail different mails at the administration of the university but it was hard to figure out which was the correct one and they didn't end up being very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I couldn't tell from the websites which classes were in the right semester and tried to navigate based on previous years but still ended up switching which classes I took once I arrived because one of the ones I signed up for just never happened.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Good luck. Bologna would have been a 10/10 experience if it wasn't for the really poor organization.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think I took two masters and three bachelor courses, although maybe it was 1 to 4 instead.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All the teaching was centered around lectures with virtually no exercise classes, assignments or in general any good exam prepping.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Italian Culture
Algebraic Topology
Mathematical Logic
Mathematical Programming
Probability Models / Stochastic Processes

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Italian Culture, a lot of other exchange students.

questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, food is very cheap both in supermarkets and dining out (compared to Copenhagen), but locally protected products like parmesan and balsamic vinegar are obviously still pricy (but worth it ;) )

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There wasn't really anything on campus other than auditoriums, barely even any space for independent studying on campus, no friday bars or such

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just figure things out with the other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bologna has a perfect location for travelling around Italy as basically all roads and train lines pass through. Day trips to Venice, Verona and San Marino as well as maybe longer trips otherwhere in Italy like Rome, Naples and the Alps are all very doable and worth it

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, Bologna as a city is incredibly oriented towards student life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Coming from Denmark I'm not used to people walking in bike lanes, cycling on the pavement and drivers just not being aware of other road users which was incredibly frustrating. Public transportation in Bologna is also pretty slow and unreliable but often not necessary as almost all of the huge medieval center is walking distance from the main square.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: FOOD, FOOD, FOOD. Bologna is one of the top foodie cities in Europe and is home to some of the most internationally and locally loved dishes / food products like tagliatelle al ragù, lasagne and mortadella. And a whole bunch of other delicious stuff in the region of Emilia Romagna like parmesan cheese, balsamic vinegar, nocino and piadina

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't expect things to be coordinated in the same way, or very coordinated at all
Make sure to try and meet people through big event managing sites like ESN
Do be afraid to spend money on good food and travel, it is ALWAYS worth it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pizza Casa

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to connect with so many nice people from different places and travelling with them

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything logistic/bureaucratic

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
